evals.prompt: I need to parse a large JSON response (about 5MB) in Flutter without blocking the UI. What's the recommended way to do this in modern Dart?
evals.expected_output: Use Isolate.run() — it's the modern preferred API (Dart 2.19+) for one-shot tasks. It's preferred over compute(). Annotate the entry function with @pragma('vm:entry-point'). The function must be top-level or static.

assertions.text: Response recommends Isolate.run() as the preferred modern API for one-shot tasks (not compute() as primary recommendation)
Response mentions the entry point function must be top-level or static
Response mentions @pragma('vm:entry-point') annotation to prevent AOT tree-shaking

evals.prompt: My team is debating what should go in isolates. Should we put our Dio HTTP requests in an isolate? What about image resizing? Database queries with Drift?
evals.expected_output: HTTP requests (Dio) should NOT go in isolates — they're already async/non-blocking. Drift/ObjectBox handle their own isolates internally. Image resizing SHOULD go in an isolate — it's CPU-intensive. The rule: if it takes >16ms on the main thread, isolate it.

assertions.text: Response correctly states network requests (Dio) should NOT go in isolates — they are already non-blocking async
Response correctly identifies image processing/resizing as a good use case for isolates (CPU-intensive)
Response correctly notes Drift (or ObjectBox) handles its own isolate management internally

evals.prompt: I'm using isolates to process items in a list. The user can navigate away before processing completes. How do I cancel in-progress isolate work when the widget is disposed?
evals.expected_output: Uses worker_manager with cancelable tasks. Cancel the cancelable in BLoC close() or widget dispose(). Shows workerManager.execute() returning a CancelableOperation. Cancel on navigation away.

assertions.text: Response uses worker_manager (or similar) with cancelable task execution
Response cancels the isolate work in dispose() or BLoC close() — not leaving it running after widget is gone
